entries.literature: Tetrodotoxin blocks voltage-gated Na+ channels; neurons cannot fire.
entries.mechanism: A dose-dependent fraction of neurons gets ttx_frac (cannot spike).
entries.prediction: Firing falls toward zero; the fly stops (only residual body drive remains).
entries.title: TTX silences the brain and the body

entries.literature: Tetanus toxin light chain cleaves synaptobrevin and blocks transmitter release; the standard genetic tool for silencing neuronal output in Drosophila (Sweeney et al. 1995, Neuron).
entries.mechanism: motor_out goes to 0 (motor neurons fire but nothing reaches the legs).
entries.prediction: Firing unchanged, movement falls toward zero. The mirror image of P1.
entries.title: Tetanus toxin: brain lit, body frozen

entries.literature: Volatile anaesthetics (isoflurane) produce dose-dependent loss of responsiveness in flies that reverses on washout; recovery time grows with dose.
entries.mechanism: GABA-A potentiation (g_inh up) and reduced background drive (I_bg down).
entries.prediction: Firing and activity fall under the drug and recover as concentration decays; higher dose means longer recovery.
entries.title: Anaesthesia is dose-dependent and reversible

entries.literature: Picrotoxin (GABA-A antagonist) is a standard convulsant in Drosophila seizure models; the signature is synchronous population bursting.
entries.mechanism: g_inh falls toward ~0.1 of baseline at dose 1.0.
entries.notes: Diagnosis recorded: the network is drive-dominated, not inhibition-stabilised, so removing inhibition releases almost nothing; seizures also need a slow variable the model lacks. Proposed fix is a two-population model, not attempted.
entries.prediction: Firing rises and synchrony spikes sharply; navigation collapses.
entries.title: Picrotoxin: removing inhibition causes seizure-like bursting

entries.literature: Caffeine increases waking activity and reduces sleep in flies (Shaw et al. 2000, Science; Hendricks et al. 2000, Neuron).
entries.mechanism: Adenosine-receptor antagonism modelled as background drive (I_bg) up.
entries.notes: Weak test by design: nearly follows from the mechanism. Included for the dose-response curve, not as strong evidence. Model has since gained glial tone scaling (numbers shifted, direction kept).
entries.prediction: Firing and activity rise, monotonic with dose.
entries.title: Caffeine increases locomotor activity

entries.literature: Low ethanol doses increase locomotion, high doses sedate — a robust biphasic curve in Drosophila (Wolf, Rodan, Tsai & Heberlein 2002; Parr et al. 2001). The low-dose stimulation depends on dopamine and octopamine signalling.
entries.mechanism: Deliberately single-class: GABA-A potentiation, depressed excitatory transmission, added membrane noise. No neuromodulatory system.
entries.notes: The mismatch is the finding: it supports the literature claim that the stimulant phase needs a second mechanism. Second hypothesis (global excitability gain for octopamine/dopamine tone) to be added only after this result, labelled as new.
entries.prediction: Monotonic decrease with dose: sedation reproduces, low-dose hyperactivity does not.
entries.title: Ethanol: biphasic locomotion (expected to fail)

entries.literature: Gaudry et al. 2013, Nature: ipsilateral ORN release is ~30-40% stronger, giving PNs a bilateral comparison. Real flies navigate odour mainly by wind direction (Alvarez-Salvado et al. 2018).
entries.mechanism: Real connectome wiring, ORN to descending neurons; 1.3/0.7 ipsilateral release bias.
entries.notes: Signal dies at the first synapse on all three connectome flies under raw weights; median in-degree normalization revived LI to LH/MB (+0.04) but legs show ipsi==contra exactly (fully mixed). Klinotaxis rejected (MB slope uncorrelated with approach; 40-run record CAN'T TELL). Wind direction dies centrally too. Three steering hypotheses rejected; the missing computation is now precisely mapped.
entries.prediction: A left/right smell difference should at least reach the lateral horn with measurable bias.
entries.title: Does the real wiring steer toward the banana?

entries.literature: DEET makes attractive odours less attractive to real flies (Ditzen et al. 2008).
entries.mechanism: Odour-receptor inhibition: smell-driven input to receptor neurons falls.
entries.prediction: Receptor firing and banana-finding fall; whole-brain firing nearly unchanged.
entries.title: DEET repels from the nose

entries.literature: Citronellal-class repellents (library expectation; aversion itself not modelled).
entries.mechanism: Chemicals that excite ORNs regardless of odour (I_sens_bg drive).
entries.prediction: Receptor-neuron firing rises while bananas found falls: the banana is drowned out, not hidden.
entries.title: Citronellal / PMD drown out the banana

entries.literature: Pyrethroid knock-down shape (library expectation).
entries.mechanism: Sodium-channel action (see library entry).
entries.prediction: Firing and activity rise at low dose, silence at high dose (depolarising block).
entries.title: Permethrin knock-down shape

entries.literature: Transporter drugs raise dopamine signalling (library expectation).
entries.mechanism: Dopamine transporter substrates; dopamine release gain (g_DA) up.
entries.notes: Behavioural direction deliberately unpredicted while the P7 steering problem stands; only firing-based measures count.
entries.prediction: Firing changes through dopamine neurons, FlyWire brain only.
entries.title: Amphetamine / cocaine / bupropion act via dopamine neurons

entries.literature: Taste is not modelled (library rule).
entries.mechanism: None: the lab refuses to dose them.
entries.prediction: Dosing is refused with an explanation, never faked.
entries.title: Sugar and salt are refused

entries.mechanism: Dosed dopamine raises drive into dopamine-receptor neurons (I_bg plus dopr mask from held expression data).
entries.notes: Machinery proof, not a real-fly validation: shows the targeted routing works and the random brain stays inert.
entries.prediction: Dopamine-receptor firing rises on connectome brains; nothing happens on the random brain.
entries.title: Receptor-targeted dopamine routing

entries.mechanism: Per-region glial tone follows firing; methylxanthine boosts scale from half (rested) to full (tired).
entries.notes: Machinery proof with a falsifiable shape: caffeine hits harder on tired brains. Absolute tone numbers are assumptions.
entries.prediction: Tone tracks activity and resets; clamped-tired caffeine beats clamped-rested with identical noise.
entries.title: Glial tone scales caffeine

entries.mechanism: Adenosine arm low (I_bg, ec50 0.1), PDE arm higher (g_exc, ec50 3.1); 31x ratio from ChEMBL medians (n=108+20). Ordering from mammalian pharmacology, strength/steepness assumed.
entries.notes: Machinery proof with a testable join point: the PDE arm passes 10% engagement at dose ~1.8 and never saturates in 0..2.
entries.prediction: Low doses are adenosine-only; the PDE arm joins higher and lifts firing further.
entries.title: Theophylline dual mechanism

entries.mechanism: Declared exposure days speed clearance (x1.2 per day, methylxanthines; assumption).
entries.notes: Machinery proof: exact clearance math plus falling day-4 lift. Sensitivity (pharmacodynamic) tolerance not built.
entries.prediction: Clearance matches half-life/1.4 at 2 days; day-4 lift sits below day-0.
entries.title: Tolerance by declared exposure
Light reaches the eye and moves the visual targets
entries.literature: Fly photoreceptors release histamine, which inhibits the lamina targets (Hardie 1989, and textbooks since). Real flies also steer toward dim light (phototaxis).
entries.prediction: Lamp on raises photoreceptor firing on all brains; direct visual targets are suppressed on Maxime (histamine-labelled) and driven on Hagrid (mostly unlabeled, default excitatory) — a data-quality divergence, flagged. No behaviour predicted: steering is unbuilt (P7).
entries.mechanism: Lamp gradient (0..1 per side) times visual-drive gain I_vis 2.0 into photoreceptor channels (R1-6/R7/R8 types). Direct visual targets = non-photoreceptors getting >25% of input current from photoreceptors (BANC 2,244; Male CNS 2,821). Raised background drive 2.2 lifts targets off the firing floor so inhibition is visible.
entries.notes: Three layers buried this effect: the firing floor, whole-group averaging (photoreceptors are 1.7% of optic-lobe current on average), and photoreceptor-to-photoreceptor edges. Rule 1 (measure what acts) is what found it. Records: light-vs-dark SUPPORTED on both sexes (photoreceptors); visual-targets card MIXED (Maxime suppressed, Hagrid driven).

entries.title: ninaE nulls are blind
entries.literature: ninaE encodes the R1-R6 rhodopsin; nulls cannot phototransduce (O'Tousa et al. 1985, Cell).
entries.prediction: Silencing photoreceptors kills the lit-vs-dark gap on visual targets while sparing the rest of the brain.
entries.mechanism: ninaE_ko lesions the photoreceptors group (BANC 1,849; Male CNS 5,160) via the lesion mask; cleared by restore.
entries.notes: Cross-check vs Alliance PHENOTYPE (4,709 annotations): top terms rhabdomere/retina/ommatidium/photoreceptor neuron + abnormal visual behavior — MATCHES (blind). Records: MIXED: photoreceptors to zero both sexes; Hagrid targets fall (predicted), Maxime targets rise (disinhibition — her photoreceptors are inhibitory). The miss confirms the Vision V1 sign split.

entries.title: Orco nulls are anosmic
entries.literature: Orco is the obligate olfactory coreceptor; nulls lose OR-mediated smell (Larsson et al. 2004, Neuron).
entries.prediction: Silencing nose ORNs kills the banana-smell response while sparing the rest.
entries.mechanism: Orco_ko lesions the nose group (simulable banana-ORN subset only, stated).
entries.notes: Cross-check vs Alliance PHENOTYPE (894 annotations): top term abnormal smell perception (102x) + abnormal chemosensory behavior — MATCHES (anosmic). Some mammalian inferred terms present (ignored). Records: SUPPORTED both sexes: nose to zero with banana present.

entries.title: para nulls cannot spike
entries.literature: para encodes the voltage-gated sodium channel pore; nulls are embryonic lethal with no evoked activity (Loughney et al. 1989, Cell).
entries.prediction: Brain-wide lesion silences all firing, like TTX; the null beside the para_ts hypomorph preset.
entries.mechanism: para_ko lesions every neuron; cleared by restore.
entries.notes: Cross-check vs Alliance PHENOTYPE (3,949 annotations): paralytic/heat-sensitive (268x), bang sensitive, abnormal neurophysiology, lethal — MATCHES direction (unexcitable; real flies paralyze where the sim goes silent). Records: SUPPORTED both sexes: null silences 100%, hypomorph quiets ~70% — allelic series reads cleanly.

entries.title: Gr66a nulls are bitter-blind
entries.literature: DEET is sensed as bitter by Gr66a gustatory neurons (Lee, Kim & Montell 2010, Curr Biol).
entries.prediction: Zeroing the bitter arm removes bitter suppression of taste firing while sweet stays identical.
entries.mechanism: Gr66a_ko preset sets bitter_gain 0 (param, not lesion: the sim pools sweet+bitter GRNs).
entries.notes: KO4 SUPPORTED both sexes: taste firing +299% Maxime / +166% Hagrid vs bitter WT (unsuppressed). Map names the GNG (+23%/+15%), the gustatory center.

entries.title: DEET contact route moves taste firing (sweet-confounded)
entries.literature: Same Gr66a-bitter paper as E-Gr66a; S3 co-locates DEET bitterness with the banana (assumption).
entries.prediction: Predicted taste firing lower in the DEET box (bitter suppresses).
entries.mechanism: S3: dose DEET pins the bitter drop on the banana at min(1, amount); I_taste 2.0 both boxes.
entries.notes: MISMATCH on the card prediction, model vindicated: Hagrid taste firing ROSE +111% (NOT SUPPORTED), Maxime +16% null. Cause: sweet (+1.0) outweighs bitter (-0.5) at shared contact, and DEET-box flies held closer to the banana (7.89 vs 9.57). GNG +11% in Hagrid map confirms the taste system activated. Lesson: contact taste is position-confounded; pure-bitter KO4 remains the clean test.

entries.title: Rdl disinhibits the brain (epilepsy proxy)
entries.literature: Rdl encodes the Drosophila GABA-A receptor; loss leaves the brain disinhibited (lab gene note).
entries.prediction: Halving inhibitory gain raises whole-brain firing; seizures themselves not modelled.
entries.mechanism: Rdl preset sets g_inh 0.5 (DAT_null precedent for param presets).
entries.notes: D1 SUPPORTED both sexes: +18% Maxime / +119% Hagrid whole-brain. Map: LAL/AVLP/slopes up (Maxime), AVLP/LAL/cord up ~200% (Hagrid) — disinhibition hits motor-adjacent regions hardest.

entries.title: park nulls lose dopamine firing (Parkinson proxy)
entries.literature: park/Pink1 nulls progressively lose dopaminergic neurons (lab disease note; graded assumption, no expression map).
entries.prediction: Lesioning half the dopamine neurons roughly halves dopamine firing; rest of brain intact.
entries.mechanism: park entry: ko_groups dopamine neurons + ko_frac 0.5 (deterministic first-half lesion).
entries.notes: D2 SUPPORTED both sexes: -58% Maxime / -57% Hagrid, matching the 50% lesion. Hagrid map: mushroom body -57% (heavily dopamine-innervated). No synuclein/mitochondria/tremor modelled.

entries.title: Taste channel: bitter arm, S3, Gr66a preset
entries.prediction: Bitter suppresses taste firing in WT only; DEET doses pin bitterness on the food.
entries.mechanism: bitter_gain param (default 1.0) scales the bitter arm; World.deet_bitter/clear_deet_bitter (S3); I_taste pinned 2.0 by calibration (sweet 0.35%->10.63% banc, 0.77%->11.73% malecns).
entries.notes: TEST 6 (bitter gap vanishes, sweet bit-identical) + TEST 10 (S3 co-location, cap, release).

entries.title: Disease V1: Rdl preset + ko_frac partial lesions
entries.prediction: Rdl raises firing; park halves DA firing with central alive.
entries.mechanism: lesion_for supports ko_frac (sorted first fraction, validated 0..1); Rdl {g_inh: 0.5}.

entries.title: Cocaine on DAT nulls (occlusion the sim cannot show)
entries.literature: Cocaine blocks dDAT (Porzgen et al. 2001); without the transporter there is nothing to block (occlusion logic).
entries.prediction: Model predicts higher dopamine firing (gains multiply); biology predicts no added effect.
entries.mechanism: DAT_null preset (g_DA 1.5x) + cocaine handles (g_DA up to 2.5x); no drug-needs-target logic exists.
entries.notes: Record SUPPORTED both sexes (+59%/+43%) = the declared mismatch. Value: proves exactly which logic is missing.

entries.title: Gr5a nulls are sweet-blind
entries.literature: Gr5a marks sweet gustatory neurons (labellar/tarsal bristles; lab gene note).
entries.prediction: Zeroing the sweet arm removes the sweet lift; bitter intact.
entries.mechanism: Gr5a_ko preset sets sweet_gain 0 (param, not lesion: pooled GRNs).
entries.notes: KO5 first CAN’T TELL (rare contact = wide spread); KO5b at 20/box SUPPORTED both (-96%/-80%). GNG down on the map.

entries.title: Gr63a nulls are CO2-blind
entries.literature: Gr21a/Gr63a is the ab1C CO2 receptor (glomerulus V; lab gene note).
entries.prediction: Silencing CO2 ORNs kills the CO2 response to zero.
entries.mechanism: Gr63a_ko lesions CO2 ORNs (91 banc / 55 malecns); manual provenance.
entries.notes: KO6 SUPPORTED both: CO2 firing -100%/-100%.

entries.title: nompC nulls are wind-blind
entries.literature: nompC is a mechanotransduction channel of chordotonal/JO neurons (lab gene note).
entries.prediction: Silencing wind sensors kills the wind response to zero.
entries.mechanism: nompC_ko lesions wind sensors (2132 / 4291); manual provenance.
entries.notes: KO7 SUPPORTED both: wind firing -100%/-100%; Maxime map nerve cord/GNG down.

entries.title: per01 misses the daylight lift
entries.literature: per01 nulls are arrhythmic (no functional PERIOD; lab mutant note).
entries.prediction: Over a day-biased run, rhythmic WT averages more drive: per01 lower firing, higher sleep fraction.
entries.mechanism: circa_amp 0.3 both boxes (1440-step day, runs cover dawn->midday); per01 preset forces amp 0.
entries.notes: C1 SUPPORTED both sexes both measures: firing -75%/-46%, sleep 0.00->0.55. Partial-day window only; period/phase need longer runs.

entries.title: Caffeine tolerance over 4 declared days
entries.literature: Metabolic tolerance by faster clearance (model assumption, Phase 3; fly methylxanthine tolerance data may not exist).
entries.prediction: Four prior days shrink the caffeine firing lift (clearance x1.8).
entries.mechanism: set_exposure verb + induction k=0.2 on methylxanthines; declared on the card.
entries.notes: T1 SUPPORTED both: -9%/-4% with zero spread. Small sizes, real gaps; resolves at endpoints per TEST 17.

entries.title: Bupropion wired curve reads net-inhibitory
entries.literature: DAT/NET inhibition + nicotinic antagonism, both mammalian (entry evidence); DAT ratio 4.21x cocaine from ChEMBL.
entries.prediction: Predicted DA firing higher at 1.5 (wired ec50 1.68).
entries.mechanism: DAT/NET arms at ec50 1.68; nAChR arm at 0.6 (assumption). g_DA scales release, not excitability.
entries.notes: MISMATCH on expectation, wiring vindicated: -6%/-18% DA firing, regions -25-40%. The ACh arm (x0.79) beats the DAT arm at every dose. Follow-up: measure downstream/activity or rebalance arms from data.
